_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its (non-)oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.stdio.semio.graph` is a semio-NATIVE format — no third party reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` for it, so no oracle is registered (see noOracleDecisions below).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: There is no third-party crate that reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, let alone one authoritative over this subset's `SemioGraphMutation` vocabulary (create/delete-node, change-node-kind, change-node-label, move-node, add/remove-node-port, add/remove-node-property, create/delete-edge) — that vocabulary IS this subset's own specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. Confidence instead comes from the committed, independently handcrafted per-kind fixtures under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — a `(before, mutation, after, diff)` specification vector per kind, authored by hand and already unit-tested inside the production crate itself (`kinds_match_the_enum_and_the_catalog`, `produces_committed_diff`, `committed_diff_applies_to_after`, `committed_json_is_canonical` per leaf) — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a mutation and then its own computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation fixture (order-insensitive over the id-keyed `nodes`/`edges` sets, since `create-node`/`create-edge` always append). This feature re-exercises those SAME committed fixtures end-to-end through `apply_semio_graph_mutation`, the entry point this ticket added, rather than calling `Mutation::diff`/`inverse` directly as the in-crate unit tests do.
